cards.title: Simultaneous small size and low degree in semialgebraic refutations
cards.formal: Can a small refutation in Sums-of-Squares (SOS), Positivstellensatz (PS), or Sherali–Adams (SA) be replaced by a refutation in the same system that simultaneously has the degree supplied by the size-to-degree theorem and controlled monomial size? The input is an unsatisfiable finite system of real polynomial inequalities and equalities on n Boolean variables, with maximum constraint degree k, and a refutation of monomial size S. For SOS the known degree target is O(k+√(n log S)); for PS of product width at most w it is O(kw+√(n log S)). The source asks whether this can be attained without a size explosion. It does not quantify the permitted size increase or whether algorithmic conversion is required, so the recovered question is not yet a single fully specified proposition.

cards.definitions: Use commuting variables x₁,…,xₙ and their formal twins x̄₁,…,x̄ₙ over R. The Boolean ideal Iₙ is generated by xᵢ²−xᵢ, x̄ᵢ²−x̄ᵢ and xᵢ+x̄ᵢ−1 for every i. Thus the intended assignments have xᵢ∈{0,1} and x̄ᵢ=1−xᵢ. Input constraints are qⱼ≥0 and pᵢ=0, given as finite sums of real coefficients times monomials. An SOS refutation is an identity −1≡s₀+Σⱼsⱼqⱼ+Σᵢtᵢpᵢ modulo Iₙ, where each sⱼ is explicitly represented as Σₐrₐ,ⱼ² and tᵢ is arbitrary. It certifies that no intended assignment satisfies all constraints. In the cited 2019 convention its monomial size is the sum, with multiplicity across polynomials, of the numbers of nonzero monomials in all rₐ,ⱼ and tᵢ. Its degree is the maximum of deg(s₀), deg(sⱼ)+deg(qⱼ), and deg(tᵢ)+deg(pᵢ) over nonzero terms. Coefficient bit lengths and the multipliers of Boolean axioms are not counted. A PS refutation additionally allows terms sⱼ to multiply products Π_{j∈J}qⱼ; its product width is max|J|, and the corresponding degree includes Σ_{j∈J}deg(qⱼ). The same multiplier-based size convention excludes expansion of those input products. An SA certificate has the SOS identity’s shape but s₀ and sⱼ are polynomials with nonnegative coefficients, hence nonnegative on Boolean assignments; arbitrary squares of sums are unavailable. SA monomial accounting must specify whether it counts only these multipliers and tᵢ, or also input and Boolean-axiom polynomials, as distinguished in the 2022 thesis. The question concerns sparse monomial representations rather than arithmetic circuits or binary encodings of rational coefficients. The number of variables, constraint degrees and, for PS, product width are parameters; degree reduction alone gives no prescribed bound on the new certificate’s monomial size.
cards.answer_criterion: After specifying the allowable size bound and whether the target is existential or algorithmic for the named system, establish both that size bound and the degree bound for the same refutation on every eligible input, or refute that universal statement. Separate proofs witnessing small size and low degree do not meet the target. Tightness of the degree-only theorem is a different question. The current passage leaves the acceptable size increase unspecified, and this review does not substitute a chosen polynomial bound.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.
